claim: In 100 retrospective internal-medicine error cases, cognitive factors were present in 74% and system factors in 65%; only 28% were cognitive-only. A thinking scaffold can address at most the cognitive part.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; use as a scope limit. Report gains only on reasoning-step failures, not on missing-test or handoff failures.

claim: Within cognitive errors, faulty synthesis dominates (about 264 of 320 instances), premature closure is the most common single named cause (39, about 12%), and knowledge deficits are rare (11, about 3%). Single study, coded after the fact.
agent_test: On a closure-prone case set, compare adding knowledge hints versus adding a closure check (is any listed alternative still without a discriminating check) at equal tokens.

claim: Telling clinicians to slow down, be careful or reflect does not raise diagnostic accuracy (44.5% vs 45.0%, n=204; first-impression vs directed-search instruction p=.12, n=393). Wrong diagnoses take longer, not shorter.
agent_test: Plain prompt vs same prompt plus 'be slow and thorough' at equal tokens on the same cases; expect no gain.

claim: Teaching bias names, cognitive forcing strategies or debiasing checklists did not reduce errors in controlled human trials (191 students; 61 ECG readers; review conclusion).
agent_test: Named-bias checklist prompt vs baseline at equal tokens; expect null.

claim: Contested: a systematic review reports guided reflection as the most consistently successful intervention, while the forcing and checklist trials and a real-patient checklist pilot (error 11.2% vs 17.8%, p=.46) were null.
agent_test: Arm A no recheck, arm B generic forcing line, arm C structured reanalysis of code-listed findings, equal tokens.

claim: Structured reanalysis of case findings recovered accuracy after an induced availability bias (second-year residents 1.55 vs 2.19 on similar vs other cases; reflection raised similar-case scores to 2.03). No control group redid cases without reflection.
agent_test: Plant a prior similar case in context; compare fresh-context re-derivation from raw findings vs continued same-context reconsideration.

claim: Free-form self-directed second looks help little: residents revised 8% of diagnoses and score moved 1.20 to 1.22 of 2 (n=47).
agent_test: Generic 'review your answer' pass vs no pass; measure flip rate and net accuracy change.

claim: Salient misleading findings placed early cut student accuracy by 61% (0.27 to 0.11) and shortened processing time per word; placed late they cut accuracy 36% with no time change. First direct behavioural sign of premature closure, in students.
agent_test: Insert a distractor at start vs end of a case; test whether re-presenting findings in shuffled order recovers accuracy.

claim: Anchoring in diagnosis looks like a weighing problem, not a looking problem: eye fixations did not differ, but accurate residents recalled more key findings (0.47 vs 0.20). Recall is post hoc.
agent_test: Force explicit per-finding by per-rival scoring in code vs free narrative; compare accuracy on distractor-led cases.

claim: Time limits reduce accuracy partly by cutting the number of alternative hypotheses (accuracy 0.44 vs 0.53; alternatives 0.37 vs 0.51). The actual limit matters; felt pressure did not in a second study (p=.044 borderline).
agent_test: Vary token budget; record rival-set size and accuracy; check that a minimum-rivals rule rescues the low-budget arm.

claim: Injecting a bias cue into a medical question lowers accuracy in every LLM tested (BiasMedQA, 1,273 items, 6 models). GPT-4 was most robust; weaker models lose far more. Drops are relative percentages of baseline, not points. It tests suggestibility to a stated cue, not own-trajectory closure.
agent_test: Run the agent on BiasMedQA with and without scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: A 'be aware of bias' education prompt or few-shot bias examples gives only modest, model-dependent gains in LLMs (GPT-4 frequency 0.627 to 0.720; weaker models marginal); in BiasBuster few-shot often broke the output format.
agent_test: Baseline vs awareness line on a BiasMedQA subset with a mid-size model; expect small or no gain.

claim: Numeric anchors pull GPT-3.5/4/4o; chain of thought, ignore-the-anchor, thoughts-of-principles and reflection prompts did not remove the pull. Showing two opposed anchors brought GPT-4 near the bias-free value on 8 of the 15 expert-hint questions, those where the two hints bracketed the truth.
agent_test: Give the agent one lead hypothesis vs two opposed hypotheses in context; compare drift toward the lead.

claim: Tuning and model strength do not guarantee less bias: instruction tuning increased decoy, certainty and belief bias; stronger models were still consistently anchored; a model's denial of bias is not evidence.
agent_test: Measure anchoring on our actual model and task; never rely on self-report.

claim: Revealing a task in pieces makes LLMs answer early and then rely on that wrong answer: 39% average drop from FULL to SHARDED; CONCAT kept 95.1% of FULL; a first attempt in the first 20% of turns scored 30.9 vs 64.4 in the last 20%. Reasoning models degrade too. Non-medical tasks.
agent_test: Staged-information diagnosis: restate all gathered facts in a fresh context before each answer vs continuing the thread.

claim: On SDBench (304 NEJM cases) MAI-DxO (hypothesis tracker plus challenger) took o3 from 78.6% at $7,850 to 81.9% at $4,735, 79.9% at $2,396 budgeted, 85.5% at $7,184 ensembled; physicians 19.9%. Baseline anchoring was seen by inspection, not measured; no challenger ablation. Gap search: the paper reports no role-level ablation, so which part (challenger, tracker, stewardship, checklist) carries the gain is unknown; ensembling reached 85.5% and single vs batched mode gave identical 83.9% on the test set.
agent_test: Run our single-agent scaffold on SDBench with and without a code-built counterexample search at equal cost; include an Instant Answer baseline.

claim: A multi-agent role panel (devil's advocate, facilitator) fixed initial misdiagnoses on 16 cases chosen because they were wrong (final top-2 64-76% from 0%). It does not show benefit or harm when the first answer is right. Gap search: a 2025 letter asks for a single-LLM control, and general work finds debate no better than self-consistency at equal responses.
agent_test: Mix in cases with correct first answers; measure harm from the challenger as flip rate on correct answers.

claim: Writing a differential does not by itself help LLMs: GPT-4 differential prompt 78% vs CoT 76% (n.s.); GPT-3.5 fell from 46% to 38%. A human checklist nearly doubled hypotheses considered (6.5 vs 3.4) without significant error reduction.
agent_test: Hypothesis count is not the success measure; compare generate-only vs generate-then-discriminate.

claim: Humans under-use good AI advice and over-trust wrong AI advice: GPT-4 access gave no gain (76% vs 74%, 50 physicians); planted wrong ChatGPT advice cut reasoning 14.0 points even after AI training; a disagreement-signal nudge recovered 7.6 points. The physician's own first list and the machine's answer both act as anchors.
schema_part: G5, G2 (treat prior answers as claims)
agent_test: Pass a first answer (right or wrong) into a second pass as a claim vs hide it; compare error import rates.

claim: Order of information inside an investigate-then-diagnose loop changes LLM accuracy by up to 18 points (open Llama-2-family models, 2,400 MIMIC-IV cases, 4 abdominal diseases); BiasBuster also found a primacy preference for early options.
agent_test: Shuffle information order in an SDBench-style loop; measure accuracy spread with and without canonical ordering.

claim: Most reported missed or delayed diagnoses are PE, drug reaction, lung cancer, colorectal cancer, ACS, breast cancer, stroke (each 2.6-4.5% of 583); testing-phase failures 44%, clinician assessment 32%. Graber 2005 gives no condition counts. Self-reported, no denominator.
agent_test: Keep an open-test list in code that blocks closure; test on cases where a key test is pending.

claim: No published study found measures LLM premature closure on missed common diseases specifically; SDBench and Hager et al. are nearest. The phrase 'mostly missed common diseases' is only partly supported. Gap search: MedR-Bench shows free-turn questioning did not raise recall of needed examinations (R1 43.61 to 40.67) and rare vs common diagnosis was comparable; still no direct early-stop rate.
agent_test: Build a small common-disease set (PE, ACS, stroke vignettes with a benign-looking lead) and measure early-stop rate.

claim: Reflection helps complex cases but not simple ones (interaction F(1,41)=4.48, n=42), and an observed error cause (interruptions) showed no accuracy cost in three experiments.
agent_test: Recheck on all items vs only flagged hard or disagreeing items at equal total tokens.

claim: LLMs rank a planted unlikely diagnosis first far more often than clinicians: 55.6% of 72 LLM responses vs 21.2% of resident (N=20) and 10.0% of attending (N=5) responses, OR about 4, on nine vignette pairs. Abstract only.
agent_test: Insert a wrong patient-suggested diagnosis into closure-prone vignettes; compare plain run vs a run that must find a discriminating check before ranking any suggested diagnosis first.

claim: An unguided self-review lowers accuracy and flips correct answers to wrong ones (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0); gains appear only with oracle labels. In clinical challenge, flip-to-wrong rates after a wrong challenger range from about 6% (GPT-5 variants) to 97-100% (conformist models). A challenger or recheck step needs a measured flip rate on correct answers per model.
agent_test: Run the recheck on first-answer-correct cases only and report the flip-to-wrong rate; accept the step only if it stays under the gain on first-wrong cases.

claim: More samples explain much of what multi-agent critique adds: self-consistency beats debate at equal response counts (GSM8K 88.2 at 9 vs about 83 for debate), and ensembling independent MAI-DxO panels (85.5%) beat one panel (81.9%). No test of structured reanalysis against fresh re-derivation at equal tokens exists.
schema_part: 4b (do not add a debate role without an equal-token control)
agent_test: Equal-token comparison: one structured reanalysis vs one fresh independent derivation vs plain extra sample, on closure-prone cases.

claim: Supplied clinician or user reasoning steers LLMs both ways: expert context raised correct-diagnosis inclusion in all 21 variants (+20.4 points) while adversarial context lowered it in 14 (-5.4 points); stating that the clinician is unsure recovered most of the loss. A secondary report says the AI mostly agrees when it sees the physician first (52% vs 24% full overlap).
agent_test: Tag each hint with source and confidence; test accuracy with right and wrong hints, tagged vs untagged.

claim: Gathering more history does not help LLMs unless it is consolidated: CRAFT-MD multi-turn was no better than single-turn, conversation lowered accuracy (GPT-4 0.919 to 0.854), and a summary restored GPT-3.5 (0.724 to 0.810). MedR-Bench free turns did not raise needed-exam recall and models looped.
schema_part: consolidate step before closure; open-test list
agent_test: Closure-prone staged cases: with vs without a restate-all-findings block before the final differential.

claim: Open after gap search (no study found): flip rate of a challenger on first-correct answers in diagnosis; reanalysis vs fresh derivation at equal tokens in LLMs; early-distractor order effect in experts or LLMs; which stop signal best predicts wrong early stops; post-2015 premature-closure audits with interrater agreement; Goh UK replication.
agent_test: Build the in-house tests named in K24-K28.
